summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging.
takeaways: This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills.
Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance.
Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution.
